qt: to the Commission Estelle Ceulemans (S&D), Kathleen Van Brempt (S&D), Elio Di Rupo (S&D), Bruno Tobback (S&D) Subject:

At the beginning of July 2024, Audi announced a restructuring of its Brussels site, which includes plans to potentially end the production of the Q8 e-tron and Q8 Sportback e-tron models and possibly cease operations altogether. It has already been decided that production of the Q8 e-tron will be transferred to Mexico in 2027. We are particularly concerned about the preservation of jobs and production, and safeguarding and further developing green innovative technologies and industry within Europe. The reindustrialisation of Europe needs to go hand in hand with measures that encourage local manufacturing, while continuing to deepen trade relations with other parts of the world in a mutually beneficial and fair way. In this context: 1.
How will the Commission prevent the closure or relocation of manufacturing sites crucial for our sustainable transition?
How will it support and redirect our industry (and particularly the automotive sector) towards technologies and products that are fit for the just and sustainable transition and affordable to all?
What incentives will be created for our European industry (and particularly the automotive sector) to continue to invest in local manufacturing?

(31 October 2024) The Commission is committed to preserving manufacturing in Europe while ensuring a just transition and sustainable competitiveness. It is following with high attention and concern the recent developments in the EU automotive industry. The EU is supporting the automotive industry by tackling supply chain difficulties with the Critical Raw Materials Ac t (1), the Net-Zero Industry Act (2), Battery Regulation (3) and the Chips Act (4) as well as raw materials partnerships (5). It has defined a regulatory environment to encourage the transition to smart mobility with the Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy (6), the AI Act (7), the Data Act (8) and the Cyber Resilience Act (9). The EU also provides substantial financial support for the industry’s transformation to electromobility along the whole value chain (10). Moreover, the EU has put a robust framework in place for the transition to zero-emission mobility by setting binding CO 2 targets (11) for vehicle manufacturers, which are complemented by measures aimed to ensure a fair transition (12), while recognising that further initiatives are needed to strengthen the EU’s just transition policy framework (13), with a focus on anticipation and management of change.

For instance, the Commission will monitor the socioeconomic impacts of these measures with a first progress report in 2025, including on adequate financial measures to ensure a just transition and to mitigate any negative impacts, in particular in the regions and the communities most affected. The Commission has taken note of the analysis of the automotive industry’s challenges in the Draghi report (14) and will consider further measures in the context of the announced future industrial action plan for the automotive industry.
